class: Any guard that decides whether stored data holds a secret by matching field NAMES against a list (substrings or whole words) both blocks legitimate required fields and lets real secrets through, because no name list is complete for an external API's field names.
mechanism: Round 1 substring matching rejected instrument_token (Zerodha's instrument id, needed to audit broker responses) and session_expires_at; round 2 whole-word matching accepted X-Api-Key (words join to 'xapikey'), Kite's enctoken, token, totp, mpin, while still rejecting otp_sent_at. The mechanism was added by the orchestrator's builder brief, not by any acceptance criterion.

first_seen.evidence: Verifier probes: round 1 instrument_token REJECTED; round 2 _is_secret_key('X-Api-Key') False, ('enctoken') False, ('otp_sent_at') True.

fix: Removed from the audit log (W-015 round 3). Replaced by design with a per-event-type field allowlist (REQ-063 AC-5, work item W-017, blocked until real Kite responses exist). Lesson for briefs: never ask a builder for a security mechanism no acceptance criterion defines.

detection.note: Guarded when W-017 lands with real Kite login/order response fixtures.
